newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Western bids for big Kazakh oil producer narrowed.
newsitem.headline: Western bids for big Kazakh oil producer narrowed.

text.p: Six companies have bid in a tender for Kazakhstan's largest oil producer Mangistaumunaigaz, and a shortlist has been drawn up, a State Property Committee source said on Tuesday.

The source, who declined to be identified, said Oryx Energy Co of the United States, ZAO Mangistaumunaigas, K & B of the United States, Central Asia Petroleum Ltd of Indonesia (a unit of Indonesia's Setdco Group), Neft S.A. of Russia and Vitol-Kazakhstan (a joint venture with Dutch oil trader and refiner Vitol) had submitted bids.
The Vitol-Kazakhstan, Mangistaumunaigaz and Oryx applications were rejected for unspecified reasons, and bids by Central Asia and K & B were the forerunners, the source said.
A winner would be announced after March 10.
Mangistaumunaigaz, in western Kazakhstan near the Caspian Sea, accounts for nearly one-third of annual Kazakh oil output.
The tender is for a 50-60 percent stake in the financially-troubled but promising producer.
It produced six million tonnes (120,000 barrels) of oil and 1.8 billion cubic metres of gas in 1995, the last year for which figures were available.
